# Forms and inputs (Bonus tips)

<a id="frm-01"></a>
## FRM-01 - Design fields for the type of input

Avoid one-size-fits-all inputs; shape fields to the data. For verification codes, one box per digit with large type.

- **Source:** PDF 114 (printed 113), 115 (printed 114)
- **Applies when:** Verification codes, PINs and other fixed-format inputs.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- One-size-fits-all fields are a disservice; align fields with the type of information requested to streamline interaction and remove cognitive load.
- Separate big boxes per code digit with enlarged typography minimise errors with a clearly designated space per digit, speed entry and make digits easy to distinguish, especially for users who struggle with small text.

**Mistake:** A single long standard text field for a 4-digit code.  
**Effect:** More entry errors; harder to read digits.

**Correction:** Segmented input: one box per digit, large digits.  
**Why it works:** Structure communicates the expected format.

**Observable checks:**
- Are fixed-length codes entered in a generic full-width text input?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Interpretation (ours, not stated by the PDF):**
- SUPPLEMENTAL implementation note (not from the PDF): segmented code inputs should still support paste, autofill (e.g. one-time-code autocomplete) and screen readers.

**Source issues / ambiguity:**
- SOURCE ORDER ERROR: the text calls the four-box design 'the first example', but in the figure the four-box version is on the right with the green thumbs-up and the single field is on the left with the pink thumbs-down. The lesson itself is unambiguous.

**Related:** [FRM-02](17-forms.md#frm-02), [IC-07](16-interaction-cost.md#ic-07)

<a id="frm-02"></a>
## FRM-02 - Size fields to the expected data

Match field length to the type and amount of data: short fields for CVC, expiry and ZIP, placed side by side, instead of every field full-width.

- **Source:** PDF 115 (printed 114), 116 (printed 115)
- **Applies when:** Payment, address and profile forms.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- A form with one long field per item (including CVC, expiry and ZIP) is less effective; matching field length to the data is better.
- A CVC is always 3 or 4 digits, so a shorter field is more appropriate and guides the user; the same applies to expiry date and ZIP. Concise fields remove ambiguity and use space efficiently.
- The better design aligns the input field's design with the expected data, aiding accurate and efficient entry.

**Mistake:** Every payment field stacked at full width.  
**Effect:** Ambiguity about expected length; long, inefficient form.

**Correction:** Expiry and CVC side by side as short fields; Country and ZIP side by side with a short ZIP.  
**Why it works:** Field width is a format hint.

**Observable checks:**
- Are short fixed-length inputs (CVC, expiry, ZIP, year) rendered full-width?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [FRM-01](17-forms.md#frm-01), [LAY-04](09-layout.md#lay-04), [WS-04](08-whitespace.md#ws-04)

<a id="frm-03"></a>
## FRM-03 - Replace 'confirm password' with a show/hide toggle

A second password field adds interaction cost, is error-prone and gives a false sense of security; a visibility toggle lets users check their input.

- **Source:** PDF 117 (printed 116), 118 (printed 117)
- **Applies when:** Sign-up and password-change forms.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- 'Confirm Password' fields are a common but outdated practice.
- Downsides: increased interaction cost (every extra field), error-prone (a mismatch often forces starting over) and a false sense of security (users can mistype the same way twice).
- A show/hide toggle lets users check their input without a second field, maintaining security and giving control over visibility.

**Mistake:** Enter password + Confirm password fields.  
**Effect:** Extra effort and frustrating restarts.

**Correction:** One password field with an eye/eye-slash toggle.  
**Why it works:** Users verify directly instead of typing twice.

**Observable checks:**
- Is there a 'Confirm password' field? Does the password field have a visibility toggle?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [FRM-04](17-forms.md#frm-04), [IC-07](16-interaction-cost.md#ic-07)

<a id="frm-04"></a>
## FRM-04 - Show inline password strength feedback

The source's corrected example shows a strength meter with a 'Weak password strength' label directly under the password field; its explanatory text is a duplicated paragraph.

- **Source:** PDF 119 (printed 118)
- **Applies when:** Password creation.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Heading only: 'Use inline password validation'. The paragraph repeats the show/hide-toggle text from FRM-03.

**Mistake:** Not stated by the source.  
**Effect:** Not stated by the source.

**Correction:** Interpretation of the figure: a segmented strength meter and a coloured strength label below the field, visible before submitting.  
**Why it works:** Not stated by the source; see interpretation.

**Observable checks:**
- Does the user get password feedback while typing rather than only after submitting?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Interpretation (ours, not stated by the PDF):**
- Fix and check derive from the figure only (4-segment meter, first segment red, 'Weak password strength').

**Source issues / ambiguity:**
- SOURCE ERROR: the body text under 'Use inline password validation' duplicates the show/hide toggle paragraph.

**Related:** [FRM-03](17-forms.md#frm-03), [COL-04](14-color.md#col-04)
